passages.note: Bill overview page shows he was prime sponsor of HB2492, whose short title is voter registration; verification; citizenship.
House Third Reading roll call lists him Y on a 31-26 vote, so it is not near-unanimous.

passages.provision_quote: Except for a form produced by the United States election assistance commission, any application for registration shall be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship as prescribed in section 16-166, subsection F, and the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections shall reject any application for registration that is not accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship.
passages.note: Chaptered text prints the operative citizenship-evidence requirement at registration; the bill's single subject is qualification and registration of electors.

rows.reasoning: As prime sponsor of HB2492 (2022) he voted Y on its House Third Reading, and the chaptered text requires that "any application for registration shall be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship" and that the recorder "shall reject any application for registration that is not accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship". That matches the rung "Require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote" clause for clause: proof of citizenship, demanded at registration. The House record counts for his Senate seat because it is the same legislature (V5), and the 31-26 tally is not near-unanimous.
